definition_zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；弄乱；食堂
definition_en: an untidy or dirty state; the waste left behind; a difficult situation; a group of people who eat together or the room where they eat; and as a verb, to make untidy or to spoil
core_image: 聚餐散场后，桌上盘盏堆叠，汤汁洒在桌布上，地上散落着碎屑
scene: 聚餐散场后，桌上的盘子还堆着，地毯上撒了饼干屑，厨房的门半开着。After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
sceneCN: 这里是「凌乱、脏乱」（第 1 个义项：东西没归位）；句意为聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。图中可辨识物件：堆着的盘子、地毯上的碎屑、半开的门。

pos.zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；食堂

derivatives.zh: 由 mess 加 -y 构成，义为「凌乱的；脏乱的」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ly 构成，义为「凌乱地」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「凌乱；杂乱」

senses.title: An untidy, dirty state
senses.definition: a state in which things are not in order and look dirty or untidy
senses.definitionCN: 东西没有归位、看上去又脏又乱的状态
senses.example: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
senses.exampleCN: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。
senses.why: The earliest mess was a portion of food served at table, so the modern sense of disorder still smells of the kitchen: plates, scraps and things left where they fell.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 mess 是端上桌的一份食物，所以今天「凌乱」这一义仍带着厨房气味：盘子、残渣，以及掉在哪里就留在哪里的东西。

senses.title: Dirt or waste left behind
senses.definition: dirty waste matter, especially the droppings of an animal, that somebody has to clean away
senses.definitionCN: 脏的废弃物，尤指动物的粪便，需要有人清理掉
senses.example: Watch the path, the dog leaves a mess on the grass every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 走路当心，那条狗每天早上都在草地上留下一摊脏东西。
senses.why: Once a mess is food that has been served and eaten, what remains on the ground is also a mess, so the word slides from the meal to its leftovers and then to any filth.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mess 是端上桌又被吃掉的食物，留在地上的残渣自然也是 mess，于是词义从饭菜滑向剩渣，再滑向一切脏东西。

senses.title: A difficult or confused situation
senses.definition: a situation full of trouble and confusion, especially one that someone has caused and must get out of
senses.definitionCN: 充满麻烦与混乱的局面，尤指自己造成、又必须脱身的局面
senses.example: He admitted his finances were in a mess after the failed deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那笔交易失败后，自己的财务状况一团糟。
senses.why: When things are physically out of order, affairs can be out of order too, so the untidy room grows into a tangled situation with no easy way out.
senses.whyCN: 当东西在实处乱了套，事情也能乱套，于是凌乱的房间长成一团找不到出口的局面。

senses.title: To make untidy or to spoil
senses.definition: to make something dirty or untidy, or to spoil a plan or arrangement badly
senses.definitionCN: 把东西弄脏弄乱，或把计划、安排彻底毁掉
senses.example: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: to put something into a mess, or to ruin it the way a spilled plate ruins a laid table.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：把东西弄成一团乱，或者像打翻一盘菜弄污摆好的桌面那样，把事情毁掉。

senses.title: A group that eats together, or its dining room
senses.definition: a group of people, especially soldiers, who eat together, or the room in which they eat
senses.definitionCN: 一起吃饭的一群人，尤指军人，或他们就餐的房间
senses.example: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。
senses.why: The first sense was a portion of food shared at one table; the people who shared it and the room where they shared it then took over the same name.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思是同桌分享的一份食物；一起分享的人，以及他们分享所在的房间，后来都沿用了这个名字。

intro.en: Mess began as a word for a portion of food sent to table, and it reached English through French from a Latin verb meaning to send.
intro.cn: mess 起初指端上桌的一份食物，经法语进入英语，其源头是拉丁语中表示「送」的动词。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it supplied the verb behind a large family of sending words.
items.cn: mittere 意为送、放出，是这一大批与「送」有关的词共同的动词来源。

items.en: The noun missus named a course of food served at a meal, literally something sent to the table.
items.cn: 名词 missus 指用餐时端上的一道菜，字面意思是「被送到桌上的东西」。

items.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, meaning a portion or a dish, and also a group eating together.
items.cn: 古法语 mes 保留了食物义，指一份或一道菜，也可指一起进餐的一群人。

items.en: Middle English mess first meant a dish of food and a company of diners, especially in a household or an army.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mess 先指一盘食物和一群共餐者，尤用于家庭或军队。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word toward disorder in the eighteenth century, while the dining sense survived in military usage.
items.cn: 现代英语在十八世纪把词义推向「混乱」，而就餐义则在军队用语中保存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same Latin sending root; the near-meaning group collects words for disorder and jumble.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「送」词根上的词；近义组收表示混乱与杂乱的名词。

entries.definition: Untidy, dirty or complicated, said of rooms, hair or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 凌乱的、脏的或复杂的，可用于房间、头发或局面。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, from the same verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 送给某人的一条信息，同出「送」这一动词。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 把消息从一处送到另一处的人。

entries.definition: An object thrown or fired, literally something sent.
entries.definitionCN: 被投出或射出的物体，字面即「被送出的东西」。

entries.definition: A lack of order, often on a larger scale than a messy room.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏秩序，范围常比凌乱的房间更大。

entries.definition: A mass of small things lying about and taking up space.
entries.definitionCN: 散乱堆放着、占地方的一堆小东西。

entries.definition: Complete confusion in which nothing can be controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底失控的混乱。

entries.definition: A confused mixture or a state of muddled thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 混杂的一团，或思路不清的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of sending; its family keeps returning to food sent to a table, the people around it, and the disorder left when the meal ends.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「送」的动词上，同族词反复回到端上桌的食物、围桌的人，以及餐后留下的凌乱。

normal.en: Mittere in Latin means to send, and missus was a dish sent to the table.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，missus 就是被送到桌上的一道菜。

normal.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, so English mess first meant a portion or a dish, not a dirty room.
normal.cn: 古法语 mes 保留食物义，所以英语 mess 起初指一份或一道菜，而不是脏屋子。

normal.en: Because diners shared one dish, mess also named the group and the room where they ate, a sense still used in the army.
normal.cn: 因为同桌分食，mess 也指共餐的一群人与他们就餐的房间，这一义在军队中仍在用。

normal.en: Messy adds -y, meaning full of mess, and therefore untidy.
normal.cn: messy 加 -y，意为「充满 mess」，因此是凌乱的。

normal.en: Mess up is the verb phrase that turns the noun into the act of spoiling something.
normal.cn: mess up 这一动词短语把名词变成「把事情毁掉」的动作。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a shared dish now means disorder, which suggests mess is always what a good meal leaves behind.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指共享菜食的词如今指混乱，这说明混乱往往是一顿好饭留下的残局。

abstract.en: The same word covers the food, the people eating it and the room they sit in, three parts of one ordinary evening.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖了食物、吃饭的人与他们坐的房间，这是一个寻常夜晚的三个部分。

abstract.en: Calling a situation a mess borrows the picture of a table after dinner, because trouble is easier to bear when it looks like crumbs.
abstract.cn: 把局面称作 mess，是借用了餐后桌面的画面，因为麻烦一旦看起来像碎屑，就比较好承受。

examples.en: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
examples.cn: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。

examples.en: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
examples.cn: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。

examples.en: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
examples.cn: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没洗」——碗没洗，厨房就乱成一团；记住 mess 是混乱。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是送到共享桌上的一份食物；义项从饭菜扩到残渣，再到凌乱、困境，以及一群人吃饭的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table after a party, plates stacked high, gravy spilt on the cloth and crumbs scattered across the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚餐散场后的桌面，盘盏高高堆起，汤汁洒在桌布上，碎屑散落一地。

branches.cn: 聚餐后堆满盘子的水池

branches.en: crumbs and greasy marks across a table
branches.cn: 满桌碎屑与油痕

branches.en: a shoe scraping something off the grass
branches.cn: 鞋底在草地上蹭掉脏东西

branches.en: a desk buried under unsigned papers

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of sending, its noun for a dish served, the French form, and English endings that build an adjective and a noun of state.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「送」的拉丁动词、指上桌菜食的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词与状态名词的英语词尾共同支撑。

definition_zh: 消息；信息；要旨；咨文；发消息
definition_en: a piece of information sent to someone; the central idea that a speech, book or film wants to convey; a formal official communication; and as a verb, to send a message to someone
core_image: 一块钉在村口的公告板，纸条边角被风吹起，几个人凑近读上面的字
scene: 村口的公告板前围了几个人，纸上写着一行字，边角被风吹得卷起。She read the message twice before walking home.
sceneCN: 这里是「消息、留言」（第 1 个义项：传给别人的信息）；句意为她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。图中可辨识物件：公告板、纸条、卷起的边角。

derivatives.zh: 由 message 的词干加 -er 构成，义为「送信人；信使」
由 message 去 e 加 -ing 构成，义为「消息发送；即时通讯」

senses.title: Information sent to someone
senses.definition: a piece of information, news or a request that one person sends to another
senses.definitionCN: 一个人传给另一个人的一条信息、消息或请求
senses.example: She read the message twice before walking home.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。
senses.why: Latin mittere meant to send, so a message is literally the thing sent; the word names the content by the act of carrying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送」，所以 message 字面上就是「被送出的东西」；这个词是用「传递」这一动作来给内容命名的。

senses.title: The central idea of a speech or work
senses.definition: the main point or lesson that a speech, book, film or advertisement wants its audience to take away
senses.definitionCN: 演讲、书籍、电影或广告希望受众记住的核心观点或教训
senses.example: The message of the film is that small kindnesses travel further than grand promises.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的要旨是：细小的善意比宏大的承诺传得更远。
senses.why: If a message is what is sent, then a work of art also sends something, and the word shifts from the paper to the point the author wants delivered.
senses.whyCN: 既然 message 是被送出的东西，艺术作品也在送出东西，于是词义就从那张纸转到作者想送达的那层意思。

senses.title: A formal official communication
senses.definition: a formal written or spoken statement sent by a government, a leader or an organization to a body or the public
senses.definitionCN: 政府、领导人或组织向机构或公众发出的正式书面或口头说明
senses.example: The president sent a message to Congress on the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 总统就新预算向国会提交了一份咨文。
senses.why: Because sending is neutral, the same word can serve ceremony as well as chat, and officials borrowed it for statements that must be on record.
senses.whyCN: 因为「送」本身是中性的，同一个词既可服务闲谈也可服务仪式，官方便借它来指必须留档的说明。

senses.title: To send a message to someone
senses.definition: to send a written or electronic message to a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 向某人或某个群体发送书面或电子信息
senses.example: He messaged the whole team as soon as the train stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 火车一停，他就给全队发了消息。
senses.why: Once the noun names the thing sent, it easily becomes a verb: people began to message each other as soon as a channel existed.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指的是被送出的东西，它就很容易变成动词：一有了传递渠道，人们就开始互相 message。

intro.en: Message comes from the same Latin verb as mission and missile, and it reached English through French as the name for what is sent.
intro.cn: message 与 mission、missile 同出一个拉丁动词，经法语进入英语，本义就是「被送出的东西」。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, to dispatch or to let go, and it stands behind mission, missile and message alike.
items.cn: mittere 意为送、派遣、放出，mission、missile 与 message 都由它而来。

items.en: The participle missus meant sent, and the derived noun named a sending or something dispatched.
items.cn: 分词 missus 意为「送出的」，由它派生的名词指一次发送或被送出之物。

items.en: Medieval Latin missaticum named a message or an errand, literally the business of one who is sent.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 missaticum 指消息或差事，字面是被派出者所办的事。

items.en: Old French message meant news or a communication carried by word or letter, and it entered English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 message 指口头或书信传递的音信，诺曼时期之后进入英语。

items.en: Modern English widened message to the point of a film, then narrowed it again to texts and chats when new channels appeared.
items.cn: 现代英语把 message 扩展到作品的要旨，等到新渠道出现，又把它收回到短信与聊天上。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin sending family; the near-meaning group collects short communications and written notices.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「送」的词族；近义组收简短的通信与书面通知。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message between two places.
entries.definitionCN: 在两地之间传递消息的人。

entries.definition: A formal or humorous word for a letter that is sent.
entries.definitionCN: 对「发出的信件」的正式或戏谑说法。

entries.definition: A portion of food sent to table, later disorder; the same sending verb lies behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 端上桌的一份食物，后来指混乱；背后的动词同样是「送」。

entries.definition: A task or journey given to someone who is sent to do it.
entries.definitionCN: 交给被派出者去完成的差事或行程。

entries.definition: A short written record or a few lines left for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录，或留给某人的几行字。

entries.definition: A short internal notice sent between members of an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 组织成员之间传阅的简短内部通知。

entries.definition: A written or printed statement that tells people something.
entries.definitionCN: 告知人们某事的书面或印刷说明。

entries.definition: The broader act of passing information, by speech, writing or signal.
entries.definitionCN: 通过说话、书写或信号传递信息的更宽泛行为。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of sending; its family keeps returning to what is dispatched, who carries it, and the point it is meant to deliver.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「送」的动词上，同族词反复回到被送出之物、送它的人，以及它想送达的那层意思。

normal.en: Mittere in Latin means to send, so a message is the thing that has been sent.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，所以 message 就是被送出去的那样东西。

normal.en: Missaticum in medieval Latin named an errand or a message, the business of a person who is sent.
normal.cn: 中世纪拉丁语的 missaticum 指差事或消息，即被派出者要办的事。

normal.en: Messenger adds -er to the same stem, naming the person who carries the message.
normal.cn: messenger 在同一词干后加 -er，指送消息的人。

normal.en: Message and mess share the verb mittere, one naming what is sent, the other the dish sent to a table.
normal.cn: message 与 mess 共用 mittere，一个指被送出的东西，一个指送到桌上的菜。

normal.en: Get the message is the idiom built on arrival: the information has reached you and you understand it.
normal.cn: get the message 这一成语建立在「送达」上：信息到了你这里，你也懂了。

abstract.en: A word for a thing sent shows that meaning always needs a carrier, a route and a receiver before it counts as communication.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「被送出之物」的词说明：意思必须先有载体、路线与接收者，才算完成了传递。

abstract.en: The same word covers a note, a film and a presidential address, because all three ask someone to receive something.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖便条、电影与总统咨文，因为三者都在请人接收某样东西。

abstract.en: When the phone lit up, the old noun quietly became a verb, proof that a word changes shape when a new channel appears.
abstract.cn: 手机亮起时，这个古老的名词悄悄变成了动词，证明新渠道出现时词也会改换形态。

examples.en: She read the message twice before walking home.
examples.cn: 她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。

examples.en: The message of the film is that small kindnesses travel further than grand promises.
examples.cn: 这部电影的要旨是：细小的善意比宏大的承诺传得更远。

examples.en: He messaged the whole team as soon as the train stopped.
examples.cn: 火车一停，他就给全队发了消息。

root: 拉丁语 mittere（送）→ missus（送出的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 missaticum（差事、消息），经古法语 message 进入英语；同族词多与传送、派遣有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something sent from one person to another; the senses divide into a piece of news, the point a work delivers, an official statement and the act of sending.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从一个人送到另一个人的东西；义项分为一条音信、作品要送达的意思、官方说明，以及发送这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board nailed up at the entrance of a village, a paper note flapping at the corner, a few people leaning in to read it.

branches.cn: 职员隔着桌子递出封好的信

definition_zh: 方法；办法；条理；体系；（学科或艺术的）方法论体系
definition_en: a particular way of doing something, especially one that is planned and systematic, or the order and system that such a way produces
core_image: 一条被反复踩出的小路：草被踩平了，路指向远处的目标
scene: 老实验室里的那套流程几十年没有变过。The lab still uses a method that has not changed in forty years.
sceneCN: 这里 method 是「方法」（第 1 个义项：做某事的特定程序）；句意：这个实验室仍在使用一套四十年没变过的方法。场景要点：一排贴着编号的旧仪器、墙上手写的步骤表、被踩得发亮的地面；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A way of doing something
senses.titleCN: 方法：做某事的特定路数
senses.definition: a particular procedure for doing something, especially a planned and systematic one
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的特定程序，尤指有计划、有系统的程序
senses.example: The lab still uses a method that has not changed in forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验室仍在使用一套四十年没变过的方法。
senses.why: Method reached English in the early 15th century from Greek methodos, originally 'pursuit, a following after'. A method is a path that has already been walked and can be walked again.
senses.whyCN: method 于 15 世纪初从希腊语 methodos 进入英语，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。方法就是一条已经被人走过、还可以再走一遍的路。

senses.title: Orderliness
senses.definition: the quality of acting in an orderly, systematic way rather than at random
senses.definitionCN: 做事有条理、有系统，而非随意的品质
senses.example: There was method in the way she sorted the files, though no one else could see it.
senses.exampleCN: 她整理文件的方式自有章法，只是别人看不出来。
senses.why: From the 1610s the word also named 'orderliness, regularity'. The path is no longer a particular route but the habit of always walking on one.
senses.whyCN: 自 17 世纪 10 年代起，这个词也指“有条理、有规律”。此时路不再是一条具体路线，而是“总要沿着某条路走”的习惯。

senses.title: A complete system
senses.definition: a complete set of rules or procedures for attaining an end
senses.definitionCN: 为达到某一目的而设的一整套规则或程序
senses.example: The school adopted a new method for teaching reading.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采用了一套新的阅读教学体系。
senses.why: The sense 'a system or complete set of rules' is recorded from the 1680s. Once a path is written down as rules, it can be taught to strangers.
senses.whyCN: “体系或完整规则集”这一义项自 17 世纪 80 年代有记录。一旦一条路被写成规则，它就能教给陌生人。

senses.title: Scientific method
senses.titleCN: 科学方法：学科自己的路
senses.definition: the established procedure of a discipline for testing claims and producing knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科为检验主张、生产知识而确立的程序
senses.example: The scientific method is less a single recipe than a set of habits of doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 科学方法与其说是一份单一配方，不如说是一组怀疑的习惯。
senses.why: Greek methodos already meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry'. Science did not invent the word; it inherited the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 methodos 本就意为“科学探究、探究的方法”。科学没有发明这个词，它继承的是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Teaching and acting methods
senses.titleCN: 教学法与表演体系：一门手艺的路
senses.definition: a named system of practice in teaching or in the arts, such as the direct method or method acting
senses.definitionCN: 教学或艺术中以人名或特征命名的实践体系，如直接教学法、方法派表演
senses.example: Method acting asks the performer to draw on real memories.
senses.exampleCN: 方法派表演要求演员调动真实的记忆。
senses.why: A system with a name becomes a school. Method here is a path that a whole profession agrees to walk together.
senses.whyCN: 一套有名字的体系会变成一派。这里的 method 是一整门行业同意一起走的那条路。

senses.title: Old medical sense
senses.titleCN: 医学旧义：系统化的治疗方案
senses.definition: in early use, the regular, systematic treatment of disease
senses.definitionCN: 在早期用法中，指对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗
senses.example: The medieval physician spoke of a method for fevers, not a single remedy.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的医生讲的是治疗热病的一套方法，而不是某一味药。
senses.why: The first English sense, in the early 15th century, was 'regular, systematic treatment of disease'. The word entered through medicine before it belonged to everything else.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的第一个义项是 15 世纪初的“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”。这个词先通过医学进来，然后才属于一切别的事物。

senses.title: Method in programming
senses.titleCN: 编程中的方法：对象身上的函数
senses.definition: in object-oriented programming, a function or procedure attached to an object or class
senses.definitionCN: 在面向对象编程中，附着于对象或类上的函数或过程
senses.example: The method returns a new list instead of changing the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法返回一个新列表，而不修改旧列表。
senses.why: The metaphor survives in code: a method is still a fixed route the object knows how to take when it is called.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在代码里活了下来：方法仍是对象被调用时知道该怎么走的一条固定路线。

senses.title: A method of inquiry
senses.titleCN: 探究之路：哲学意义上的方法
senses.definition: in philosophy, the deliberate path of doubt or reasoning by which a conclusion is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，为抵达结论而有意采取的怀疑或推理之路
senses.example: Descartes began with a method of doubt that would leave only certainty standing.
senses.exampleCN: 笛卡尔从一种怀疑的方法开始，只为留下确定的东西。
senses.why: Methodos was literally a following after something. Philosophy turns that pursuit into a rule for how to pursue anything at all.
senses.whyCN: methodos 字面上就是“跟在某物之后追”。哲学把这趟追寻变成一条规则，规定该怎样追寻任何东西。

senses.title: Method in one's madness
senses.definition: in the phrase 'there is method in one's madness', used when apparently foolish behaviour turns out to have a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 「there is method in one's madness」 中，指看似荒唐的行为其实自有目的
senses.example: He shuffles the cards for ten minutes, but there is method in his madness.
senses.exampleCN: 他把牌洗了十分钟，看似荒唐，其实自有章法。
senses.why: Shakespeare's phrase 'though this be madness, yet there is method in it' (Hamlet) gave English a fixed way to say that a path is hidden inside chaos.
senses.whyCN: 莎士比亚的句子“though this be madness, yet there is method in it”（《哈姆雷特》）给了英语一个固定说法：混乱里藏着一条路。

intro.en: Method is Greek: meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road, way'. Latin borrowed it as methodus and passed it to French and English. It has no connection with medical, despite the shared -met- shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: method 是希腊词：meta“追寻”加 hodos“路、道”。拉丁语把它借作 methodus，再传给法语和英语。尽管有共同的 -met- 外形，它与 medical 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'regular, systematic treatment of disease', through Latin methodus 'way of teaching or going' and Greek methodos.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 15 世纪初，意为“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”，经拉丁语 methodus“教学或行走之道”与希腊语 methodos 而来。

items.en: Greek methodos meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry, investigation', and originally 'pursuit, a following after'.
items.cn: 希腊语 methodos 意为“科学探究、探究的方法、调查”，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。

items.en: The word joins meta 'in pursuit or quest of' and hodos 'a way, path, track, road', also 'a journey'. Hodos is of uncertain origin; Beekes suggests PIE *sod- 'course', and it is traditionally linked to Slavic words for 'course'.
items.cn: 这个词由 meta“追寻、求索”与 hodos“路、路径、轨道、道路”（也指“旅程”）组合而成。hodos 的来源不确定；Beekes 提出原始印欧语 *sod-“行程”，传统上也把它与斯拉夫语表示“行程”的词联系起来。

items.en: The sense widened to 'any way of doing anything' in the 1580s, to 'orderliness, regularity' in the 1610s, and to 'a system or complete set of rules' in the 1680s.
items.cn: 词义在 16 世纪 80 年代扩展到“做任何事的方式”，17 世纪 10 年代扩展到“有条理、有规律”，17 世纪 80 年代扩展到“体系或完整的一套规则”。

items.en: The phrase method acting is recorded in reference to the theory associated with the Russian director Konstantin Stanislavski.
items.cn: method acting 这一说法有记录，指与俄国导演康斯坦丁·斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基相关的理论。

items.en: Medical goes back to Latin medicus 'physician', with no Greek element. Meta- in method is the Greek preposition 'in pursuit of', not the modern prefix meaning 'beyond' or 'after'; the two words only share letters.
items.cn: medical 追溯到拉丁语 medicus“医生”，不含希腊语成分。method 里的 meta- 是希腊语介词“追寻”，不是现代表示“超越、之后”的前缀；两个词只共享字母。

note.en: The first group is the word family built on method: the adjective, the adverb and the study of method. The second group compares the nouns English uses for 'a way of doing something', which differ in scale and in who owns the way.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 method 上的词族：形容词、副词与研究方法的学问。第二组比较英语里表示“做某事的方式”的几个名词，区别在于尺度大小与“这条路归谁”。

entries.definition: the branch of knowledge that studies methods, or the set of methods used in a field. It is not a longer synonym of method: a methodology can contain several methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究方法的学问分支，或某一领域所使用的一套方法。它不是 method 的加长同义词：一套方法论里可以包含好几种方法。

entries.definition: done according to a method; orderly and systematic. It describes a person or a procedure, not a route.
entries.definitionCN: 按方法进行的；有条理、有系统的。它描述人或程序，而不描述一条路线。

entries.definition: in an orderly, step-by-step way. It answers 'how', while method answers 'by what route'.
entries.definitionCN: 有条理地、一步一步地。它回答“怎样做”，而 method 回答“走哪条路”。

entries.definition: to reduce something to order or system. The verb turns the noun into an action; it is rare outside formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物整理成秩序或体系。这个动词把名词变成动作；在正式写作之外很少见。

entries.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or subject, often including the attitude behind it. It is broader and softer than method, which implies explicit steps.
entries.definitionCN: 处理问题或课题的方式，常包含背后的态度。它比 method 更宽、更软，而 method 暗示明确的步骤。

entries.definition: a particular way of carrying out a single task, especially one requiring skill. Techniques are the small parts inside a method.
entries.definitionCN: 完成单项任务的具体方式，尤指需要技巧的那种。technique 是 method 内部的一个个小零件。

entries.definition: a thing or resource used to achieve an end. Means answers 'with what'; method answers 'in what order'.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而使用的东西或资源。means 回答“用什么”，method 回答“按什么顺序”。

entries.definition: an established or official sequence of steps. It is more bureaucratic than method and often written down by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的或官方的步骤顺序。它比 method 更带行政色彩，常由某个权威写下来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road', the Latin borrowing methodus, and the family methodical, methodology, methodize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”、拉丁语借词 methodus，以及 methodical、methodology、methodize 词族。

normal.en: hodos means 'road'. A method is literally 'a following after on a road': meta plus hodos.
normal.cn: hodos 意为“路”。method 字面上就是“沿路跟随”：meta 加 hodos。

normal.en: In method, meta- does not mean 'beyond' or 'after' as it does in modern English; it means 'in pursuit of'. The Greek preposition is about chasing, not about position.
normal.cn: 在 method 里，meta- 不像现代英语那样表示“超越”或“之后”，而是“追寻”。这个希腊语介词讲的是追赶，不是位置。

normal.en: Methodology is not a fancy word for method: it is the study of methods, or the whole set of them used in a field.
normal.cn: methodology 不是 method 的高级说法：它是对方法的研究，或某一领域所使用的整套方法。

normal.en: Methodical describes the person who always walks on a path; method names the path itself.
normal.cn: methodical 描述那个总沿着路走的人；method 命名的是那条路本身。

normal.en: Medical looks similar but is Latin medicus 'physician'. One word has a road in it, the other has a doctor.
normal.cn: medical 看着像，其实是拉丁语 medicus“医生”。一个词里装着一条路，另一个词里装着一位医生。

abstract.en: Picture grass in a field. One path is visible because many feet chose the same line; that line is a method.
abstract.cn: 想象一片草地。有一条路看得见，是因为许多脚选择了同一条线；那条线就是 method。

abstract.en: A path can be walked by one person or written down for a school. The moment it is written down, method becomes methodology.
abstract.cn: 一条路可以由一个人走，也可以写下来给一个学派。写下来的那一刻，method 就变成了 methodology。

abstract.en: Method is the order of steps, not the tool in your hand. A hammer is a means; how you swing it is a technique; the sequence is the method.
abstract.cn: method 是步骤的顺序，不是你手里的工具。锤子是 means；怎么挥是 technique；先后次序才是 method。

examples.en: No method will save a study that was badly designed in the first place.
examples.cn: 如果一项研究一开始就设计得很糟，任何方法都救不了它。

examples.en: She works without method, yet somehow finishes before everyone else.
examples.cn: 她做事毫无章法，却总能比别人先做完。

examples.en: The two laboratories use different methods and keep getting different numbers.
examples.cn: 两个实验室用不同的方法，得到的数字也一直不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卖瑟德”——卖瑟德把一条踩出来的小路画在纸上，卖给后来的人照着走 → method 方法、办法（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自希腊语 methodos“追寻、探究”，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，核心是“沿着一条路追到目标”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of method, all from one image: a line worn into the grass by feet that wanted the same destination. It can be one path, the habit of taking paths, or the written map of them.
sensesIntro.cn: method 的九个义项都来自同一幅画面：一条被想抵达同一目标的脚踩出来的草径。它可以是某一条路、走路的习惯，或被写下来的路线图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path worn into grass, pointing at a destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被踩进草地的小路，指向某个目的地。

branches.en: THE PATH: the oldest senses name a procedure, first for curing disease, then for anything at all.
branches.cn: 路：最老的义项命名一套程序，先用于治病，后用于任何事。

branches.en: THE HABIT: orderliness is walking on a path by choice, and the idiom says a path may hide inside apparent chaos.
branches.cn: 习惯：条理是有意识地沿路走；那条习语则说，混乱里也可能藏着一条路。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: written rules turn a path into a teachable system, and science inherits the oldest 'inquiry' sense.
branches.cn: 体系：写下来的规则把路变成可教的体系，而科学继承的是最古老的“探究”义。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: teaching and acting give the path a proper name, and philosophy makes the pursuit itself a rule.
branches.cn: 学派：教学与表演给这条路一个专名，哲学则把追寻本身变成规则。

branches.en: THE CODE: in software the object still knows a fixed route to take when called.
branches.cn: 代码：在软件里，对象被调用时仍知道该走哪条固定路线。

intro.en: Method is a Greek compound borrowed whole: meta- plus hodos 'road'. English adds -ical, -ically, -ology, -ologist and -ize, while the same hodos builds episode, period and Exodus.
intro.cn: method 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：meta- 加 hodos“路”。英语加上 -ical、-ically、-ology、-ologist、-ize，而同一个 hodos 还构成 episode、period、Exodus。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek word unchanged as methodus 'way of teaching or going', and Late Latin methodicus came from Greek methodikos. Latin had its own word for 'way', modus, but method did not come from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样吸收希腊词作 methodus“教学或行走之道”，晚期拉丁语 methodicus 来自希腊语 methodikos。拉丁语自己表示“方式”的词是 modus，但 method 并非来自它。

items.meaning: a following after on a road; a way of doing something
items.meaningCN: 沿路追寻；做某事的方法（meta- 追寻 + hodos 路）
items.example: They tried every method and failed with each.
items.exampleCN: 他们试了每一种方法，每一种都失败了。

items.meaningCN: 按方法进行的；有条理的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: His methodical notes filled four notebooks.
items.exampleCN: 他条理分明的笔记写满了四个本子。

items.meaningCN: 有条理地；一步一步地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 她逐个抽屉有条理地检查。

items.meaning: the study of methods; a set of methods used in a field
items.meaningCN: 方法论；一套研究方法（-ology 表学问）
items.example: The paper was rejected for its weak methodology.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文因方法论薄弱而被拒。

items.example: The two studies differ on methodological grounds.
items.exampleCN: 这两项研究在方法上存在分歧。

items.meaning: a specialist in methods of research
items.example: A methodologist was added to the review panel.
items.exampleCN: 评审组里增加了一位方法论专家。

items.meaning: to arrange according to a system
items.meaningCN: 使有条理；使系统化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: He methodized the archive over one winter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一个冬天把档案整理成体系。

items.meaning: a member of the Protestant denomination founded at Oxford in 1729
items.meaningCN: 卫理公会教徒（-ist 表追随者，源于其讲究方法的修行方式）
items.example: The Methodist chapel still stands on the corner.
items.exampleCN: 卫理公会礼拜堂仍立在街角。

items.structure: epi- (besides) + eisodos (a coming in, from hodos 'way')
items.meaning: an incident or instalment inserted into a larger whole
items.meaningCN: 插曲；（系列中的）一集（epi- 另外 + eisodos 进入，含 hodos 路）
items.exampleCN: 最后一集什么也没解答。

items.meaning: a going round; a length of time
items.meaningCN: 周期；一段时间（peri- 环绕 + hodos 路，即“绕一圈”）
items.example: The period lasted almost a century.
items.exampleCN: 这一时期持续了将近一个世纪。

items.meaning: a going out; a mass departure
items.meaningCN: 出走；大批离去（ex- 向外 + hodos 路）
items.example: The drought set off an exodus from the villages.
items.exampleCN: 旱灾引发了村庄的大批出走。

items.meaning: a performance technique that draws on the actor's own experience
items.meaningCN: 方法派表演（以体系命名的表演技术）
items.example: Method acting changed how American films were shot.
items.exampleCN: 方法派表演改变了美国电影的拍摄方式。

definition_zh: 米；韵律
definition_en: the British spelling of the unit of length, or the rhythm of beats in poetry
core_image: 诗行旁标着音步，桌上还放着一把一米长的木尺
scene: 诗行旁标着音步，桌上还放着一把一米长的木尺。The pool is twenty metres wide.
sceneCN: 这里 metre 是「米」（第 01 个义项）；句意是泳池宽二十米；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 公制的
韵律的

senses.title: The British spelling of the unit of length
senses.definition: The British spelling of the unit of length
senses.definitionCN: 公制长度单位的英式拼写
senses.example: The pool is twenty metres wide.
senses.exampleCN: 泳池宽二十米。
senses.why: Metre is the British form of Greek metron, a measure; English kept this spelling for the unit of length.
senses.whyCN: metre 是希腊语 metron（尺度）的英式拼法，英语用它表示长度单位。

senses.title: The rhythm or pattern of beats in poetry
senses.definition: The rhythm or pattern of beats in poetry
senses.definitionCN: 诗歌中节拍的格局
senses.example: The poem is written in a slow metre.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗用了缓慢的韵律。
senses.why: The same Greek word named a measure of sound, so metre also came to mean the measured beat of verse.
senses.whyCN: 同一个希腊词也指声音的尺度，于是 metre 又指诗句中被量出的节拍。

intro.en: The history of metre is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: metre 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Metron meant a measure.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为尺度。

items.en: The measure became the metre.

definition_zh: 中间；中部；中期；腰部；中间的；中等的；中间派的
definition_en: the central point or part of something, the middle period of a process, the waist, or an adjective meaning central or moderate
core_image: 一条长桌的正中摆着一只花瓶，两侧的椅子对称排开
scene: 长桌两端都坐满了人，只有正中的位置还空着，等着最后到的那位客人。She cut the cake down the middle and gave half to each child.
sceneCN: 这里 middle 是「中间、正中」（第 1 个义项：距离两边同样远的位置）；句意为她沿着正中把蛋糕切开，分给每个孩子一半。画面里可抓住的物件：长桌、空着的正中座位、切开的蛋糕。

pos.zh: 中间的；中等的；中间派的

senses.title: The central point or part
senses.definition: the point or area equally far from the edges or ends of something
senses.definitionCN: 距离边缘或两端同样远的那一点或那一带
senses.example: There is a fountain in the middle of the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场中央有一座喷泉。
senses.why: Old English middel was built with the suffix -el from a root for middle, much as a small tool is made from a larger one; the word names the place that divides a length into equal halves.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 middel 由表示「中间」的词根加后缀 -el 构成，就像用一个较大物件做出小工具；这个词指的就是把一段长度分成相等两半的位置。

senses.title: The middle of a period or process
senses.definition: a point in time when an event or process is half done
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件或过程进行到一半的时间点
senses.example: The project ran into trouble in the middle of the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目在夏季中期遇到了麻烦。
senses.why: Because the central point can be laid on time as well as on space, the same word covers the halfway stage of a season, a story or a negotiation.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个中心点既能放在空间上，也能放在时间上，同一个词便覆盖了季节、故事或谈判进行到一半的阶段。

senses.title: The waist
senses.definition: the narrow part of the body between the chest and the hips, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指胸部与臀部之间身体较窄的部分
senses.example: He tied the rope around his middle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把绳子系在腰上。
senses.why: A body is widest at the shoulders and hips and narrows between them, so the word for the central part came to name the waist with no metaphor beyond shape.
senses.whyCN: 人的身体在肩与臀处最宽，中间收窄，于是表示「中部」的词就用来指腰，除了形状之外并没有额外的比喻。

senses.title: Halfway between two positions
senses.definition: placed or ranked between two other things, neither first nor last
senses.definitionCN: 处在另外两者之间，既不在最前也不在最后
senses.example: Put the tallest child in the middle row.
senses.exampleCN: 把最高的孩子安排在中间那一排。
senses.why: The noun turned adjective by standing before another noun; middle row simply means the row that sits between the front and the back.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前面就转成了形容词；middle row 指的就是夹在最前与最后之间的那一排。

senses.title: Moderate in politics or opinion
senses.definition: holding views that avoid the extremes of left and right, or of any strong division
senses.definitionCN: 持避免左右极端或任何强烈对立的观点
senses.example: The paper speaks to middle voters who dislike both extremes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸面向不喜欢两个极端的中间选民。
senses.why: A political spectrum is imagined as a line with two ends, so the party or voter near its centre is called middle; the spatial image is simply carried into public life.
senses.whyCN: 政治光谱被想象成一条有两个端点的线，靠近中心位置的党派或选民就被称为 middle；空间的形象就这样搬进了公共生活。

intro.en: Middle is the full form of the old root that also gives the short word mid; its history runs from a prehistoric root, through Old English, into everyday modern senses such as waist and moderate politics.
intro.cn: middle 是古老词根的完整形式，短词 mid 也出自同一来源；它的历史从史前词根出发，经古英语，一直走到今天「腰部」与「温和政治」这类日常义项。

items.en: The reconstructed root *medhyo- meant middle and is the common ancestor of English middle and Latin medius.
items.cn: 重构词根 *medhyo- 意为「中间」，是英语 middle 与拉丁语 medius 的共同祖先。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as *midilaz or *medilaz, a noun and adjective for the central part of something.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中的形式一般重构为 *midilaz 或 *medilaz，是表示某物中部的名词与形容词。

items.en: Old English middel added the suffix -el to the root, giving a full adjective and noun beside the shorter midd.
items.cn: 古英语 middel 在词根后加后缀 -el，在较短的 midd 之外提供了一个完整的形容词与名词。

items.en: Middle English kept middel and middle side by side, and the noun already covered space, time and the human waist.
items.cn: 中古英语中 middel 与 middle 并行使用，名词已经同时覆盖空间、时间与人的腰部。

items.en: Modern English settled on middle, extended it to social and political moderation, and kept it in fixed phrases such as middle class and middle age.
items.cn: 现代英语最终确定拼写为 middle，把词义扩展到社会与政治的温和立场，并保留在 middle class、middle age 这类固定说法中。

normal.en: Old English added -el to the root, a suffix that also appears in words for small tools, so middle is a built form rather than a bare root.

normal.en: The phrases middle class and middle age show how easily the spatial word moves into social life.

normal.en: In the middle of is the everyday frame: whatever follows it is the thing being cut into two halves.

abstract.en: Middle is a balancing word: it keeps both ends at the same distance and refuses to choose.

definition_zh: 可能；也许；（语气委婉）可以；力量；威力
definition_en: used to say that something is possible but not certain; used in careful requests and suggestions; used with have of something that was possible but did not happen; and as a noun, great physical strength
core_image: 一个人攥紧拳头，把全身的力气压进一条绷紧的绳索
scene: 仓库的门被风吹得砰砰作响，几个工人合力抵住一扇即将倒下的木门，肩膀紧紧压住门板。He pushed with all his might against the swinging door.
sceneCN: 这里是「力量、气力」（第 4 个义项：身体的力气）；句意为他用尽全力抵住那扇摇动的门。图中可辨识物件：抵门的肩膀、晃动的门板、仓库门。

derivatives.zh: 由 might 加 -y 构成，义为「强大的；有力的」
由 mighty 去 y 加 -ily 构成，义为「有力地；非常」
由 mighty 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「强大；威力」

senses.title: Possibility that something is true or may happen
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible, though the speaker is not certain it is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事有可能发生或成立，但说话人并不确定
senses.example: It might rain before we reach the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到车站之前可能会下雨。
senses.why: Might is the past form of may, and English uses a past form to make a statement sound less sure, so the word moves from permission to a guarded guess.
senses.whyCN: might 是 may 的过去式，而英语常用过去形式让陈述听起来不那么确定，于是这个词从「许可」转向「留有余地的猜测」。

senses.title: A polite request or a hesitant suggestion
senses.definition: used to ask for something or suggest an action in a careful, polite way
senses.definitionCN: 用于小心、客气地提出请求或建议
senses.example: Might I borrow your umbrella for an hour?
senses.exampleCN: 我可以借你的伞用一个小时吗？
senses.why: The same past form softens the demand; by placing the request in a distant tense, the speaker leaves the listener free to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过去式把要求放软：把请求放进一个较远的时态里，就等于给听者留下拒绝的余地。

senses.title: A past possibility that was not taken
senses.definition: used with have to say that something was possible or should have happened but did not
senses.definitionCN: 与 have 连用，表示某事本来可能发生或本该发生，却没有发生
senses.example: You might have told me the meeting had moved.
senses.exampleCN: 你本可以告诉我会议改了时间。
senses.why: Once might marks unreal possibility, adding have fixes that unreal possibility in the past, and the speaker can point at a road that was open and was not walked.
senses.whyCN: 既然 might 标记「非现实的」可能性，再接上 have 就把这种可能固定在过去，说话人便能指向一条曾经敞开、却没被走的路。

senses.title: Great physical power or strength
senses.definition: great physical strength or force, especially when gathered for a single effort
senses.definitionCN: 巨大的体力或力量，尤指为一次发力而聚集起来
senses.example: He pushed with all his might against the swinging door.
senses.exampleCN: 他用尽全力抵住那扇摇动的门。
senses.why: Before it was a modal verb, might was a noun meaning power, and the noun still keeps the older body sense that the modal has left behind.
senses.whyCN: 在成为情态动词之前，might 本是一个意为「力量」的名词；这个名词至今保留着情态动词早已丢下的、属于身体的那层意思。

intro.en: Might began as an Old English noun for power and as a past form of may, and the two meanings have stayed side by side.
intro.cn: might 起初既是古英语中表示「力量」的名词，又是 may 的过去式，这两种身份一直并存。

items.en: A reconstructed root for being able is generally proposed behind the Germanic words for power, though its exact shape remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，日耳曼语中表示「有能力」的词背后有一个重构词根，但其确切形态仍不确定。

items.en: The noun for power stood beside a verb meaning to be able, and the two supplied the family of may and might.
items.cn: 表示力量的名词与表示「有能力」的动词并列存在，二者共同供出了 may 与 might 的词族。

items.en: Old English meaht meant power, strength or ability, and miht was its variant spelling.
items.cn: 古英语 meaht 意为力量、力气、能力，miht 是它的变体拼写。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun might for power while also using it as the past form of may in conditional statements.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 might 表示力量，同时把它当作 may 的过去式，用在条件句里。

items.en: Modern English made the modal use dominant and left the noun in fixed phrases such as 「with all one's might」.
items.cn: 现代英语让情态动词用法占了主导，名词则退守到「with all one's might」这类固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family of may and might plus a compound built on mighty; the near-meaning group collects words for power and for possibility.

entries.definition: Very strong or powerful.

entries.definition: With great force, or very much.
entries.definitionCN: 以巨大的力量，或非常地。

entries.definition: Having complete power, formed from all and mighty.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有全然的力量，由 all 与 mighty 构成。

entries.definition: The ability to act or to control people and events.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或控制人与事件的能力。

entries.definition: The physical force that a body or a material can use or bear.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或材料能施展、能承受的物理之力。

entries.definition: Energy applied to move something or to make a change happen.
entries.definitionCN: 为移动某物或促成改变而施加的能量。

entries.definition: Another past-form modal used for possibility and for polite requests.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个用过去形式表示可能与委婉请求的情态动词。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two lives, a noun for bodily power and a past form of may; the family keeps returning to what a person is able to do and what may therefore happen.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词身负两重身份：一个是表示身体力量的名词，一个是 may 的过去式；同族词反复回到人能做到什么，以及因此可能发生什么。

normal.en: Might is the past form of may, and English uses a past form to sound less certain.
normal.cn: might 是 may 的过去式，英语用过去形式来让语气显得不那么确定。

normal.en: The noun might meant power long before the modal sense appeared, and the two live on in the same spelling.
normal.cn: 名词 might 在情态用法出现之前就指力量，两种身份共用同一个拼写，一直活到今天。

normal.en: The phrase 「with all one's might」 is the noun in fixed form, where might still means bodily strength.
normal.cn: 「with all one's might」是名词用法的固定形式，这里的 might 仍指身体的力量。

normal.en: Mighty adds -y to might, turning power into an adjective, and mightily adds -ly in turn.
normal.cn: mighty 在 might 后加 -y，把力量变成形容词，mightily 再在其后加 -ly。

normal.en: 「Might have done」 points at a road that was open in the past and was not taken.
normal.cn: 「might have done」指向一条过去曾经敞开、却没有被走的路。

abstract.en: A single word for power and for possibility suggests that what is possible is what a person is able to bring about.
abstract.cn: 一个同时表示力量与可能的词说明：所谓可能，就是人有能力促成的范围。

abstract.en: The modal keeps a past form to sound humble, a reminder that grammar itself can lower a voice.
abstract.cn: 情态动词用过去形式来显得谦逊，这提醒人：语法本身也能把声音放低。

abstract.en: Might have says that history holds unused doors, and the word lets a speaker stand in front of one.
abstract.cn: might have 说明过去握着一些没被推开的门，这个词让说话人站到其中一扇门前。

examples.en: It might rain before we reach the station.
examples.cn: 我们到车站之前可能会下雨。

examples.en: Might I borrow your umbrella for an hour?

examples.en: He pushed with all his might against the swinging door.

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「有能力」，它可以长成一句留有余地的猜测；义项分为可能、委婉请求、错过的过去机会，以及身体的力量。

definition_zh: 英里；很长的距离；很大的差距
definition_en: a unit of distance of about one and six tenths kilometres; a long distance in everyday speech; and a large amount or degree of difference, especially in the phrase by a mile

scene: 公路沿着荒原一直伸到天边，草丛里立着一块被风雨磨白的路碑，司机盯着它数着还有多远。The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
sceneCN: 这里是「英里」（第 1 个义项：距离单位）；句意为过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里的路。图中可辨识物件：草丛里的路碑、伸向天边的公路、远处的弯道。

senses.title: A unit of distance used in Britain and America
senses.definition: a unit of distance used mainly in the United States and Britain, equal to about one and six tenths kilometres
senses.definitionCN: 主要在美国和英国使用的距离单位，约合一点六公里
senses.example: The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
senses.exampleCN: 过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里。
senses.why: The Latin phrase behind the word meant a thousand paces, so the mile began as a counted walk rather than an abstract length.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「一千步」，所以英里最初是一段数出来的路，而不是一个抽象的长度。

senses.title: A long distance in everyday speech
senses.definition: a long way, used loosely in conversation rather than as an exact measurement
senses.definitionCN: 口语中泛指很远的距离，并不作为精确度量
senses.example: From the hill you can see the sea, though it looks miles away.
senses.exampleCN: 从山上能看见海，虽然它看上去远得很。
senses.why: Because a mile is a noticeable stretch of road, the plural easily becomes a loose word for any distance that feels long.
senses.whyCN: 因为一英里是一段能明显感觉到的路，复数形式便很容易变成泛指「任何觉得远」的距离。

senses.title: A large amount or degree of difference
senses.definition: a great amount or degree of difference, especially in the phrase by a mile
senses.definitionCN: 差距或程度很大，尤用于短语 by a mile
senses.example: Her second design was better by a mile.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第二个设计要好得多。
senses.why: A race decided by a mile is decided by a visible stretch of road, so the word turns physical distance into the size of any gap.
senses.whyCN: 以「一英里」之差决出的比赛，是靠一段看得见的路来分胜负；于是这个词把物理距离变成了任何差距的大小。

intro.en: Mile comes from a Latin phrase for a thousand paces, shortened in English to a single word for a measured stretch of road.
intro.cn: mile 来自拉丁语中表示「一千步」的短语，在英语里缩略成一个词，指一段被丈量过的路。

items.en: Mille was the Latin word for a thousand, and it stood at the head of the phrase that named the Roman mile.
items.cn: mille 是拉丁语中表示「一千」的词，也是罗马「里」这一说法开头的词。

items.en: The full phrase milia passuum meant a thousand double paces, the Roman unit for a long march.
items.cn: 完整的短语 milia passuum 意为「一千个双步」，是罗马人计量长途行军的单位。

items.en: Old English borrowed the shortened form as mil, a unit of distance used in land measurement and travel.
items.cn: 古英语借入缩短后的形式 mil，用作丈量土地与旅行中的距离单位。

items.en: Middle English mile kept the unit, but its exact length still varied from place to place.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mile 保留了这一单位，但它确切的长度在各地方仍有差异。

items.en: Modern English fixed the mile at a standard length and added loose uses such as 「miles away」 and 「by a mile」.
items.cn: 现代英语把英里的长度固定下来，并发展出「miles away」「by a mile」这类宽泛用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the mile family and one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects other units of distance and the general idea of distance.
note.cn: 形近组收 mile 的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收其他距离单位以及「距离」这一总称。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin phrase for a thousand paces; its family keeps returning to measured road, marked stones and the loose feeling of somewhere far.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「一千步」的短语上；同族词反复回到被丈量的路、立在路边的石标，以及「很远」这种宽泛的感觉。

normal.en: Mille in Latin means a thousand, and milia passuum was a thousand paces.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mille 意为一千，milia passuum 就是一千个步子。

normal.en: The Roman mile was a counted march, which is why the word feels like a stretch of road rather than a number.
normal.cn: 罗马的「里」是一段数出来的行军路程，所以这个词感觉像一段路，而不是一个数字。

normal.en: Old English shortened the phrase to mil, and English kept only the unit, not the thousand.
normal.cn: 古英语把短语缩短成 mil，英语只留下单位，丢掉了「一千」这层意思。

normal.en: Milestone joins mile to stone, a real stone set beside the road to mark each mile.
normal.cn: milestone 把 mile 与 stone 组合，指路边为标记每英里而立的真石头。

normal.en: 「Miles away」 and 「by a mile」 loosen the unit into a picture of any long distance or wide gap.
normal.cn: 「miles away」与「by a mile」把这个单位放宽成任何长距离或大差距的画面。

abstract.en: A unit built from a thousand steps suggests that early measurement was simply walking, counted and named.
abstract.cn: 一个由「一千步」构成的单位说明：早期的度量不过是走路，数出来，再给它一个名字。

abstract.en: When a fixed mile becomes miles away, a precise unit turns into a human feeling of distance.
abstract.cn: 当固定的 mile 变成 miles away，精确的单位就变成了人对距离的感受。

abstract.en: By a mile measures a gap in road lengths, a reminder that we often describe victory as travelling further.
abstract.cn: by a mile 用路的长度衡量差距，这提醒人：我们常把胜利说成「走得更远」。

examples.en: The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
examples.cn: 过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里。

examples.en: From the hill you can see the sea, though it looks miles away.
examples.cn: 从山上能看见海，虽然它看上去远得很。

examples.en: Her second design was better by a mile.
examples.cn: 她的第二个设计要好得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈尔」——迈开步子走很远，一英里一英里地数；记住 mile 是英里，也指很远。

root: 拉丁语 mille（一千）构成短语 milia passuum（一千步，即罗马里），缩略为古英语 mil，再演变为 mile；同族词多与里程、路标有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a counted march of a thousand paces; the senses divide into the fixed unit, the loose sense of a long way, and the size of a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一段数以千步计的行军路程；义项分为固定的距离单位、泛指「很远」，以及差距的大小。

definition_zh: 头脑；心智；记性；主意；留意；照看；介意
definition_en: the part of a person that thinks, feels and remembers; also memory, intention, and as a verb, to look after something or to object to it
core_image: 一个人坐在昏黄的灯下，手指按着太阳穴，屋里所有声音都退到了门外
scene: 面试进行到一半，考官忽然停下笔，问了一个与简历毫无关系的问题，房间里的空气一下子紧了。She answered without hesitation, her mind clear and quiet under the pressure.
sceneCN: 这里是「头脑、心智」（第 1 个义项：思考与感受的那部分）；句意为她在压力之下依然头脑清楚、心里安静。图中可辨识物件：考官停下的笔、摊开的简历、安静的房间。

senses.title: The thinking and feeling part of a person
senses.definition: the part of a person that thinks, feels, imagines and becomes aware of things
senses.definitionCN: 人身上用来思考、感受、想象并觉察事物的那部分
senses.example: A good question can open the mind instead of closing it.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题能打开人的头脑，而不是把它关上。
senses.why: Old English gemynd held memory and thought in one word, so the noun begins as the place where things are kept in awareness rather than as a plain synonym for the brain.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemynd 把「记忆」和「思想」放在同一个词里，所以这个名词起初指「东西被留在觉察之中的那个地方」，而不是「大脑」的简单同义词。

senses.title: To look after or keep watch on
senses.definition: to take care of a person, place or thing, or to keep watch on it for a while
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人、某处或某物，或在一段时间内看住它
senses.example: Mind the baby while I answer the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我去开门，你照看一下孩子。
senses.why: If something is held in the mind, it is being watched; from that the verb grew the sense of looking after a person or a place, as when a neighbour minds the shop.
senses.whyCN: 某物既然被放在心里，就等于被看着；动词由此长出「照看某人或某处」的意思，比如邻居替你看着店。

senses.title: To be bothered by something
senses.definition: to be troubled or annoyed by something, or to object to it, especially in questions and negatives
senses.definitionCN: 因某事而不快或恼火，或对某事表示反对，多用于疑问句与否定句
senses.example: Do you mind if I open the window?
senses.exampleCN: 我把窗户打开，你介意吗？
senses.why: To mind something in the older idiom meant to be affected by it, so the modern question about objection is really asking whether the thing touches you at all.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法里，to mind 某件事意为「被它影响」，所以现代那句询问是否反对的话，其实是在问这件事碰不碰到你。

senses.title: Memory and recollection
senses.definition: a person's memory, or the act of bringing something back into awareness
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的记性，或把某事重新带回觉察之中的动作
senses.example: Her name has slipped my mind again.
senses.exampleCN: 我又把她的名字忘了。
senses.why: Because the noun first meant what is held in awareness, losing a name is described as its slipping out of the mind, and the word keeps that sense of a store that can be searched.
senses.whyCN: 因为名词最初指「被留在觉察里的东西」，名字想不起来就说它从心里滑了出去，这个词便保留了「一个可以翻找的储藏处」这层意思。

senses.title: Intention or settled opinion
senses.definition: a decision or intention that a person has settled on, especially one that can be changed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人定下来的决定或打算，尤指还可以更改的那种
senses.example: He changed his mind about the trip at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一刻改变了出行的主意。
senses.why: A decision is what a person settles in the mind, so making up or changing one's mind treats the mind as the place where a choice is fixed or revised.
senses.whyCN: 决定是人「在心里定下来」的东西，所以下决心或改主意，都把心当作一个把选择钉住或改写的场所。

intro.en: Mind is native English rather than borrowed: an old Germanic noun for memory and thought, related through a shared prehistoric root to the Latin word for the intellect.
intro.cn: mind 是英语本族词而非借词：一个表示记忆与思想的古老日耳曼名词，通过共同的史前词根与拉丁语表示「理智」的词相连。

items.en: A reconstructed root for thinking is generally placed behind both the Latin and the Germanic words, though the exact path is inferred rather than recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构的「思考」词根同时位于拉丁语与日耳曼语这两组词之后，具体路径是推断出来的，并非有记录可查。

items.en: Latin mens meant mind or intellect and grew from that same root, which is why mental and mind are distant cousins rather than strangers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智、理智，出自同一个词根，所以 mental 与 mind 是远亲，而不是陌生人。

items.en: Germanic speakers formed a noun for memory and thought from the root; the reconstructed form is generally written with an old prefix ga-.
items.cn: 日耳曼语使用者由这个词根造出表示记忆与思想的名词，一般认为它带有一个古老的前缀 ga-，写作重构形式。

items.en: Old English gemynd covered memory, thought and the seat of both, and the ge- prefix later dropped away.
items.cn: 古英语 gemynd 兼指记忆、思想以及承载二者的所在，前缀 ge- 后来脱落。

items.en: Modern English mind keeps the noun senses of thought, memory and intention and adds verb senses of caring, watching and objecting.
items.cn: 现代英语的 mind 保留思想、记忆、意向等名词义，又添上照看、留心、反对等动词义。

normalIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, and its family keeps returning to what is held in awareness, whether that is a memory, a watch kept on something, or a view that can be changed.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼本族词，同族词反复回到「被留在觉察里的东西」——无论那是一段记忆、对某物的看守，还是一个可以更改的看法。

normal.en: Old English gemynd meant memory before it meant thought, which is why keep in mind sounds like storing something rather than reasoning about it.
normal.cn: 古英语 gemynd 先指记忆，后指思想，所以 keep in mind 听起来更像把东西存起来，而不是对它推理。

normal.en: Latin mens and English mind come from the same old root, so mental is a relative and not a borrowed stranger.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mens 与英语 mind 出自同一个古老词根，所以 mental 是亲戚，不是借来的陌生人。

normal.en: Mindful adds -ful, full of mind, and describes someone whose attention is fully present in the room.
normal.cn: mindful 加 -ful，意为「充满 mind」，形容一个人的注意力完全在场。

normal.en: Mindless adds -less, without mind, and describes action done with no thought behind it.
normal.cn: mindless 加 -less，意为「没有 mind」，形容做事背后不带思考。

normal.en: The verb mind began as keeping something in the mind, then split into watching over it and being troubled by it.
normal.cn: 动词 mind 从「把某物留在心里」出发，随后分成「看住它」与「被它困扰」两条路。

abstract.en: A word that begins as memory and ends as objection shows how much of thinking is really about what we cannot put down.
abstract.cn: 一个从记忆出发、到介意收尾的词，说明思考里有很大一部分其实是关于放不下的东西。

abstract.en: To mind a child and to mind the noise are the same verb, because care and irritation both begin with attention.
abstract.cn: 照看孩子与介意噪音是同一个动词，因为关心和恼火都从注意力开始。

abstract.en: Changing one's mind is not a failure of the word but its oldest freedom, a place where a choice can still be moved.
abstract.cn: 改主意不是这个词的失灵，而是它最老的自由——那个选择仍可被挪动的地方。

definition_zh: 分钟；片刻；会议记录；极小的；细微的
definition_en: a unit of time equal to sixty seconds; a short moment; the written record of a meeting; and, with a different pronunciation, extremely small or very detailed
core_image: 桌上小钟的秒针走完一圈，一小时被切成六十个小格
scene: 会议室门口，秘书把一叠记录纸递过来说人已到齐，主席却还在楼梯上。The chair opened the meeting a minute late.
sceneCN: 这里是「分钟」（第 1 个义项：时间单位）；句意为主席晚了很短的时间才宣布开会。图中可辨识物件：记录纸、会议室门牌、秒针。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 minute 加 -ly 构成，义为「细微地；精确地」，读作长音
由形容词 minute 加 -ness 构成，义为「微小；精细」
拉丁语 minutia 的复数，与 minute 同出 minutus（变小），义为「细枝末节」

senses.title: A unit of sixty seconds
senses.definition: a period of time equal to sixty seconds, one sixtieth of an hour
senses.definitionCN: 等于六十秒的一段时间，即一小时的六十分之一
senses.example: The film runs ninety minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片放映九十分钟。
senses.why: Latin named this unit pars minuta prima, the first small part of an hour, and the adjective minutus, made small, is the part English kept as the name of the unit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语把这个单位叫作 pars minuta prima，即「一小时的第一小部分」，其中表示「变小」的形容词 minutus 被英语保留下来，成了这个时间单位的名字。

senses.title: A short, indefinite stretch of time
senses.definition: a very short period of time, often used loosely rather than as exactly sixty seconds
senses.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间，常是模糊的说法，而不是精确的六十秒
senses.example: Wait a minute, I left the keys inside.
senses.exampleCN: 等一下，我把钥匙落在里面了。
senses.why: Once a minute names a small division of the hour, it can stand for any brief interval, because the word has already been marked as small.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 minute 指小时里的一小格，它就能代表任何短暂的间隔，因为这个词本身已经被标记成「小」。

senses.title: Extremely small in size
senses.definition: extremely small, so small that it is easy to overlook
senses.definitionCN: 极其小，小到容易被忽略
senses.example: The cracks in the glass were minute and hard to see.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃上的裂纹极小，很难看清。
senses.why: The adjective came straight from Latin minutus, made small, and it kept the literal sense of size while the noun moved off to the clock; English also gives it a long vowel, which is why the two senses sound different.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接来自拉丁语 minutus（变小），保留了字面上的尺寸义，而名词则走去指钟表上的单位；英语还让形容词读长音，所以两种义项听起来不同。

senses.title: Very detailed and precise
senses.definition: done with close attention to small details, as in a minute account or a minute examination
senses.definitionCN: 对细小之处极为留意的，如细致的叙述或细致的检查
senses.example: The report gives a minute account of the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对实验作了极为细致的记述。
senses.why: If something is so small that it needs a close look, then a close look is what the adjective also describes, so from tiny size the word slides to care about tiny detail.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物小到必须凑近才看得清，那么这种凑近的查看本身也能被同一个形容词描述，于是词义从「尺寸极小」滑向「对细处极用心」。

senses.title: The official record of a meeting
senses.definition: the written notes of what was said and decided at a meeting, usually kept in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 会议上发言与决定的书面记录，通常用复数
senses.example: The secretary took the minutes in shorthand.
senses.exampleCN: 秘书用速记做会议记录。
senses.why: Early clerks wrote the record of a meeting in very small script to save paper, and the Latin word for small gave both the script and the record its name, which is why the notes are minutes.
senses.whyCN: 早期文书为了省纸，把会议记录写得很小，拉丁语中表示「小」的词同时给了这种小字和记录本身一个名字，所以记录叫 minutes。

intro.en: Minute carries two histories in one spelling: a Latin adjective meaning made small gave both the clock unit and the adjective, and English separated them by pronunciation.
intro.cn: minute 一个拼写里装着两段历史：拉丁语中表示「变小」的形容词既生出钟表单位，也生出形容词，英语用读音把它们分开了。

items.en: Minutus meant made small, a participle of the verb minuere, to lessen, and it described anything reduced in size.
items.cn: minutus 意为「被弄小的」，是动词 minuere（减少）的分词，用来描述任何被缩小的东西。

items.en: The phrase pars minuta prima, first small part, named one sixtieth of an hour and one sixtieth of a degree, and the small-part word was carried into the unit.
items.cn: 短语 pars minuta prima 意为「第一小部分」，指一小时的六十分之一与一度的六十分之一，这个「小部分」的词后来进入了单位名称。

items.en: Old French used minute for a small written note, especially the clerk's draft of a legal or official record.
items.cn: 古法语用 minute 指小字写的便条，尤指文书对法律或公务记录的草稿。

items.en: Middle English minute named both the sixtieth of an hour and a brief moment, while the adjective small sense entered from written Latin.
items.cn: 中古英语的 minute 既指一小时的六十分之一，也指短暂的片刻；表示「小」的形容词义则从书面拉丁语进入。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun with a short vowel, the adjective with a long vowel, and the plural minutes for the record of a meeting.
items.cn: 现代英语让名词读短音、形容词读长音，并用复数 minutes 指会议记录。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root of smallness through derived adverbs and nouns; the near-meaning group gathers other words for short stretches of time.
note.cn: 形近组顺着表示「小」的拉丁词根，收派生副词与名词；近义组收其他表示短暂时间的词。

entries.definition: In tiny detail; with close attention to small parts.
entries.definitionCN: 以极细的程度；对细部极为留意地。

entries.definition: The quality of being extremely small.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的性质。

entries.definition: Extremely small, or a word form marking smallness.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；指小的词形。

entries.definition: The Latin verb meaning to lessen, listed here for the root only.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语动词「减少」，此处仅列词根。

entries.definition: A very short period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间。

entries.definition: A unit of time equal to one sixtieth of a minute.
entries.definitionCN: 等于一分钟六十分之一的时间单位。

entries.definition: A single point in time, or a very brief moment.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻；极短的瞬间。

entries.definition: A period of time, usually short and vague.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，通常短暂而模糊。

normalIntro.en: One Latin adjective for small feeds two separate words, so the family splits between clock time, tiny size and the paper record of a meeting.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「小」的拉丁形容词喂出两条不同的词路，词族因此分到钟表时间、极小尺寸与会议纸面记录。

normal.en: The time unit began as pars minuta prima, the first small part of an hour, so minute literally names a small slice of time.
normal.cn: 这个时间单位起初是 pars minuta prima，即「一小时的第一小部分」，所以 minute 字面上就是时间的一小片。

normal.en: The adjective keeps the Latin sense of minutus, made small, and English marks it with a long vowel so the ear can tell it from the clock word.
normal.cn: 形容词保留了拉丁语 minutus（变小）的意思，英语用长音标记它，让耳朵能把它与钟表那个词分开。

normal.en: Minutes of a meeting were first notes written in small script, which is why the official record shares the spelling of the small adjective.
normal.cn: 会议记录最初是用小字写下的笔记，所以正式记录与小这个形容词共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: Minutely and minuteness belong to the small adjective rather than to the time noun, and their vowels show which branch they come from.
normal.cn: minutely 与 minuteness 属于「小」的形容词，而不是时间名词，它们的元音显示了自己来自哪一支。

normal.en: Diminutive comes from the same Latin verb minuere, to lessen, so the whole family keeps returning to shrinking.
normal.cn: diminutive 出自同一个拉丁动词 minuere（减少），整个词族不断回到「缩小」这个动作。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face cut into sixty thin slices, then one slice held up close enough to show its scratches.
abstract.cn: 想象钟面被切成六十片薄片，然后取一片凑近到能看清上面的划痕。

abstract.en: The same word measures the hour and the speck of dust: smallness is the thread joining the clock to the microscope.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量一小时，也量一粒尘：小是把钟表与显微镜串起来的那根线。

abstract.en: A meeting becomes a few written pages, and those pages are named after the smallness of the handwriting that saved paper.
abstract.cn: 一场会议变成几页纸，而这几页纸得名于当初为省纸而写的小字。

examples.en: The train leaves in a minute.
examples.cn: 列车一分钟后开。

examples.en: The letters on the coin were minute and hard to read.
examples.cn: 硬币上的字母极小，很难辨认。

examples.en: She took the minutes at every board meeting.
examples.cn: 每次董事会都由她做记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你特」——迷你的本子很小，翻一页只花一分钟；记住 minute 既指分钟，也指微小的。

root: 拉丁语 minutus（变小，出自 minuere「减少」）；时间义来自 pars minuta prima（一小时的第一小部分），形容词义直接来自 minutus；会议记录义经古法语 minute（小字记录）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small piece of the hour; the senses divide into the clock unit, the vague short moment, the tiny size kept by the adjective, the close detail that size demands, and the small-script record of a meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「小时里的一小片」；义项分到钟表单位、模糊的短暂片刻、形容词保留的极小尺寸、小尺寸所要求的细致，以及用小字写成的会议记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small clock hand sweeping a circle cut into sixty narrow slices.
core.cn: 核心意象：小小的钟表指针扫过被切成六十个窄格的圆盘。

branches.en: a clock face divided into sixty slices
branches.cn: 钟面被分成六十格

branches.en: someone holding a door and saying just a moment
branches.cn: 有人扶住门说再等一下

branches.en: a crack too thin for the eye to catch
branches.cn: 细得眼睛看不见的裂纹

branches.en: a page of notes on the smallest parts of a test
branches.cn: 一页记着实验最细处的笔记

branches.en: a clerk writing the meeting in tiny script
branches.cn: 文书用小字记下会议

intro.en: Latin words for small and to lessen supply the stem, and English suffixes build the adverb, the quality noun and the family word for a small form.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「小」与「减少」的词提供词干，英语后缀则造出副词、性质名词，以及与「指小」相关的词族成员。

definition_zh: 镜子；镜面；写照；反映；映照
definition_en: a piece of glass with a reflective coating that shows images; also something that gives a faithful picture of a situation, and to show or match something as a mirror does
core_image: 晨光里的一面镜子，把窗前的人原样照回来
scene: 清晨的走廊上，她把外套领子翻正，又抬手理了理头发。She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
sceneCN: 这里是「镜子」（第 1 个义项：能照出影像的玻璃物件）；句意为面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。图中可辨识物件：镜子、衣领、走廊灯。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 mirror 加 -ing 构成，义为「镜像；反映」
由动词 mirror 加 -ed 构成，义为「装有镜子的；映出的」
由 mirror 加表示「没有」的 -less 构成，义为「无镜的」，多指相机结构

senses.title: A glass surface that shows a reflection
senses.definition: a piece of glass or polished surface with a reflective coating that shows the image of what stands before it
senses.definitionCN: 镀有反光层的玻璃或抛光表面，能照出面前事物的影像
senses.example: She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。
senses.why: The word came through Old French from a Vulgar Latin noun for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经古法语来自一个表示「照人用的玻璃」的俗拉丁名词，后者建于动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，所以物件是按它招来的那道目光命名的。

senses.title: A faithful picture of a situation
senses.definition: a person or thing that shows a situation, a period or a mood exactly as it is
senses.definitionCN: 把某种局面、时代或情绪如实呈现出来的人或事物
senses.example: The novel is a mirror of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是那个时代的写照。
senses.why: Because a mirror returns an exact image rather than a flattering one, writers use it for anything that shows a situation without distortion, and a novel can serve as that surface.
senses.whyCN: 镜子给出的是准确而非讨好的影像，作家便用它指任何不失真地呈现局面的东西，一部小说也能充当这样一面镜面。

senses.title: To show an image as a mirror does
senses.definition: to show the image of something, the way a still surface reflects what stands beside it
senses.definitionCN: 像平静表面那样把旁边的事物影像呈现出来
senses.example: The lake mirrored the pines along the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面映出岸边的松树。
senses.why: The verb was simply the noun turned into an action, so to mirror is to do what a mirror does: send back the image of whatever stands before it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是把名词直接变成动作，所以 to mirror 就是做镜子所做的事：把面前事物的影像送回原处。

senses.title: To match or correspond closely
senses.definition: to be very similar to something else, so that the two seem to copy each other
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物极为相似，看上去像彼此复制出来的一样
senses.example: The vote mirrored the national trend.
senses.exampleCN: 投票结果与全国趋势一致。
senses.why: When two patterns look identical, one seems to be the reflection of the other, so the verb widened from reflecting light to reflecting behaviour, numbers and opinions.
senses.whyCN: 当两种走势看起来一模一样，其中一个就像是另一个的倒影，于是这个动词从映出光线扩展到映出行为、数字与观点。

intro.en: Mirror comes from a Vulgar Latin name for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: mirror 来自俗拉丁语中「照人用的玻璃」这一名称，建立在动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，再经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to look at with wonder, and the looking and the wondering were not separated in the verb.
items.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，在这个动词里，「看」与「惊叹」并没有分开。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin noun, reconstructed as miratorium, named the thing one looks into; the form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语中有一个表示「供人照看的器物」的名词，学界重构为 miratorium；这是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Old French mirour carried the noun into ordinary use for the polished metal or glass a person looks into.
items.cn: 古法语 mirour 把这个名词带入日常用法，指人们照看的抛光金属或玻璃。

items.en: Middle English mirrour kept the extra vowel of the French form and also used the word for moral examples and ideal portraits.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mirrour 保留了法语形式里多出的元音，也用这个词指道德榜样与理想化的画像。

items.en: Modern English shortened the spelling to mirror, formed a matching verb, and pushed the word into talk about trends, reports and behaviour.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写缩成 mirror，造出与之相配的动词，并把这个词推进到关于趋势、报告与行为的说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for looking and wondering; the near-meaning group gathers words for reflections and for the surfaces that produce them.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词展开；近义组收表示影像以及产生影像的表面的词。

entries.definition: An optical illusion in which water seems to appear in the distance.
entries.definitionCN: 远处看似有水的一种光学幻景。

entries.definition: To look at someone with wonder and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 带着惊叹与赞许地看某人。

entries.definition: An astonishing event believed to come from divine power.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为是神力所致的惊人之事。

entries.definition: The act of reflecting an image, or of copying another's behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 映出影像的行为，或模仿他人行为的过程。

entries.definition: The image of something seen in a mirror or on water.
entries.definitionCN: 镜中或水面看到的事物的影像。

entries.definition: A hard, transparent material, or a mirror made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬透明的材料，或用它制成的镜子。

entries.definition: A picture or likeness of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 某人某物的图像或相似物。

entries.definition: To send back light or an image, or to show a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 把光或影像送回；反映某种情况。

normalIntro.en: The Latin verb for looking and wondering gives the noun, and the noun then turns into a verb, so the family keeps moving between the glass and the act of copying.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词生出名词，名词又变成动词，于是词族在镜面与复制这个动作之间来回移动。

normal.en: Mirari means to look at with wonder, and a mirror was first a looking glass, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
normal.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，而 mirror 起初就是照人的玻璃，所以这个物件按它招来的目光得名。

normal.en: Mirror, miracle, mirage and admire share that Latin verb, which is why looking and wondering sit close together in this family.
normal.cn: mirror、miracle、mirage 与 admire 共用那个拉丁动词，所以看与惊叹在这个词族里挨得很近。

normal.en: The noun came first, and to mirror is a later verb made by simply treating the object as an action.
normal.cn: 名词先出现，to mirror 是后来把这个物件直接当作动作来用才有的动词。

normal.en: Mirror image names a copy reversed left to right, the most literal use of the noun in front of another noun.
normal.cn: mirror image 指左右颠倒的复制影像，是名词放在另一个名词前最字面的用法。

normal.en: The phrase a mirror of the times still demands a faithful picture, not a flattering one.
normal.cn: a mirror of the times 这一说法仍然要求如实呈现，而不是美化。

abstract.en: Picture a still lake at dawn returning the trees exactly, without adding or hiding anything.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时平静的湖面把树影原样送回，既不增添也不隐藏。

abstract.en: A mirror can flatter or accuse, but it cannot lie about the shape in front of it; the word keeps that demand for accuracy.
abstract.cn: 镜子可以讨好也可以揭短，但它无法对面前的形状说谎；这个词一直保留着这份准确的要求。

abstract.en: To mirror someone is to become their reflection, which is why imitation and understanding can look the same from outside.
abstract.cn: to mirror 某人就是成为他的倒影，所以模仿与理解从外面看往往一模一样。

examples.en: She checked her collar in the mirror.
examples.cn: 她对着镜子整理衣领。

examples.en: The lake mirrored the pines along the shore.
examples.cn: 湖面映出岸边的松树。

examples.en: The report mirrors what workers have been saying for years.
examples.cn: 这份报告反映了工人们多年来的说法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米勒」——米勒站在镜前，镜里镜外一个样；记住 mirror 是镜子，也指反映。

root: 俗拉丁语 miratorium（照人的器物，重构形式）出自拉丁语 mirari（注视、惊叹），经古法语 mirour 与中古英语 mirrour 进入现代英语；与 miracle、mirage、admire 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a surface that returns an image; the senses divide into the glass itself, the faithful picture it stands for, the act of sending back an image, and the matching of two patterns.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把影像送回原处的表面」；义项分到玻璃物件本身、它所代表的如实写照、送回影像的动作，以及两种走势的彼此吻合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror in morning light returning the person in front of it unchanged.
core.cn: 核心意象：晨光中的一面镜子，把镜前的人原样送回。

branches.en: a hall stand with a coat and a mirror
branches.cn: 门厅里挂着外套的镜子

branches.en: a novel read as a portrait of its decade

branches.en: a faithful image and a matching pattern share one verb
branches.cn: 如实的写照与吻合的走势共用一个动词

intro.en: A reconstructed Vulgar Latin noun and the Latin verb for wondering supply the stem, and English suffixes build the adjective, the action noun and the negative form.
intro.cn: 一个重构的俗拉丁名词与表示「惊叹」的拉丁动词提供词干，英语后缀则造出形容词、动作名词与否定义的形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

provided with a mirror, or shown as a reflection
